changes.ruby: .ruby-version 3.4.12 → 4.0.9; Gemfile has no `ruby` line; Gemfile.lock has no RUBY VERSION section (unchanged)
changes.docker_base_image: ruby:3.4.12-slim-trixie → ruby:4.0.9-slim-trixie in Dockerfile.base, Dockerfile.development, Dockerfile.production; the apt line, NodeSource and nokogiri 1.19.4 pre-install are unchanged
changes.bundler: `gem install bundler -v 2.6.9` → `-v 4.0.20` in the three Dockerfiles; Gemfile.lock BUNDLED WITH 2.6.9 → 4.0.20 (now indented two spaces). Regenerated with `bundle lock` in a plain ruby:4.0.9-slim-trixie container (Bundler 4.0.20, lock only): that run changed nothing but BUNDLED WITH. No CHECKSUMS section appeared (Bundler 4 writes one only for new lockfiles or with --add-checksums; not forced). PLATFORMS aarch64-linux / ruby / x86_64-linux unchanged, re-added with `bundle lock --add-platform x86_64-linux` then `--add-platform ruby` (one per call) after every lock change
changes.bundler_frozen_flag: Bundler 4 removed `bundle install --frozen` (exit 15: 'The --frozen flag has been removed because it relied on being remembered across bundler invocations, which bundler no longer does. Instead please use `bundle config set frozen true`'). Dockerfile.ci and Dockerfile.production now run `RUN BUNDLE_FROZEN=true bundle install` — the setting scoped to that RUN, nothing written to .bundle/config. Verified both ways in the dev image: with the committed lock it reports Bundle complete; on a scratch copy with an extra Gemfile line it exits 16 with 'You have added to the Gemfile: * rack-cors … Run `bundle install` elsewhere' and leaves the lock untouched; `bundle config get frozen` shows 'Set via BUNDLE_FROZEN: true'. Not in the plan (which only named `--binstubs`), found because Dockerfile.ci was exercised locally against the local base 0.11.0
changes.gemfile_platforms: byebug line `platforms: %w[mri mingw x64_mingw]` → `%w[mri windows]` (Bundler 4: '[DEPRECATED] Platform :mingw, :x64_mingw will be removed in the future. Please use platform :windows instead'). With :windows no deprecation is printed by any bundler command. The Gemfile has a single global `source` and no `bundle install --binstubs` is used anywhere, so the other two Bundler 4 breakages in the plan do not apply
changes.erb: 4.0.4.1 → 6.0.7 via `bundle lock --update erb --conservative`. Not in the plan. Ruby 4.0.9 ships erb 6.0.7 as a default gem and it is activated before Bundler.setup runs, so with 4.0.4.1 locked every spec file failed to load: `Gem::LoadError: You have already activated erb 6.0.7, but your Gemfile requires erb 4.0.4.1. Since erb is a default gem, you can either remove your dependency on it or try updating to a newer version of bundler that supports erb as a default gem` (47 errors outside of examples, 0 examples run; the smoke specs' `cannot load such file -- nokogiri` in the same run was the same failure seen from outside Bundler). erb is only a transitive (rdoc 8.1.0 → erb); 6.0.7 is the newest release and the image's own version. cgi 0.5.2 left the lock with it — erb 6 no longer depends on the cgi gem (Ruby 4.0 removed the CGI library apart from cgi/escape). Gem count 182 → 180 (erb's duplicate default-gem copy is no longer installed separately, and cgi is gone)
changes.pathname_requires: bin/setup and bin/update: `require 'pathname'` removed. Pathname is a core class in Ruby 4.0 (`ruby -e 'p Pathname'` works on the bare image with only pathname.so in $LOADED_FEATURES), so RuboCop's Lint/RedundantRequireStatement flagged both under TargetRubyVersion 4.0 — the only two offences the new target produced. Not in the plan

lock_method: Gemfile edited first (platforms), then in a plain ruby:4.0.9-slim-trixie container with the worktree mounted: `bundle lock` (BUNDLED WITH only) → `bundle lock --add-platform x86_64-linux` → `bundle lock --add-platform ruby`; dev image built; the erb Gem::LoadError surfaced in the first ./go test; `bundle lock --update erb --conservative` → the two --add-platform calls again → dev image rebuilt.
